teaser.heading: The hand behind the needle.
teaser.lead: Born in Poland, trained in fine arts, and built on years drawing creatures for video games — Tomasz arrived at the needle by way of realism: hyperdetailed portraits, photographic skin. Then the runes found him. Then the demons followed.

chapters.title: Origin
chapters.body: Tomasz grew up in Poland, earned a master's in fine arts, and spent years as a concept artist in the video game industry — designing worlds, creatures, and characters before deciding the most honest canvas was skin. He transitioned fully to tattooing in 2015, carrying an illustrator's instinct for composition, weight, and darkness.

chapters.title: Realism
chapters.body: His first years with the machine were spent in realism. Hyperdetailed portraits, photographic skin texture, the painstaking discipline of making ink behave like light. It built his hand — taught him how skin holds tone, how depth is earned, how a needle must be trusted. But the work felt borrowed. He was translating photographs, not drawing from somewhere of his own.

chapters.title: The North
chapters.body: The pivot came through runes. Norse carving — stripped back, all line, no gradient — demanded a different kind of attention. The opposite of realism: symbolic, blunt, built for stone and permanence. His nordic period lasted years and became the spine of what he still does: the geometry, the weight, the reverence for marks that were made to outlast the hand that made them.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.body: The demonic work arrived uninvited. Nordic ornament and creature design share a root — both draw on myth, on the monstrous, on forces with names older than writing. Demons started appearing in compositions alongside runes. Not decorative: structural. The nordic thread never broke — it just tangled itself around something older and considerably less holy.

chapters.title: Studio
chapters.body: Tomasz works out of Der Grimm Tattoo in Berlin. Private chair, by appointment only. No walk-ins. The sketchy style is fast by nature — a full back piece in a single session is not unusual. His process: lay the base with magnums, apply Angel Drops before the detail pass, keep the machine moving until it's done. Sterile, single-use, and as quiet or talkative as you need it to be.
